1	=== docs/building-an-agent.md
2	# Building your agent
3	
4	Your agent system has to be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the information and makes
5	the decisions, at run time. How is up to you: drive the browser through the DOM, through pixels, or both; use one
6	model or several, in parallel if you like; give the model tools and helpers for the browser, parsing, arithmetic and
7	checks. The model chooses where to go, what to search for and which documents matter. Rejected in review: a fixed
8	script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback, and a crawler that collects the
9	websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
10	
11	## The browser
12	
13	In the sandbox a headful Chromium runs on the desktop (`DISPLAY=:1`, 1280×800) with CDP on
14	`127.0.0.1:9222`.
15	
16	- **DOM agents:** attach with Playwright (`chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`) or any CDP client.
17	- **Pixel agents:** take screenshots and send mouse and keyboard input to the desktop (`xdotool` and
18	  ImageMagick's `import` are installed), for example to drive Claude's computer-use tool.
19	- **Locally:** without `CDP_URL`, launch your own Chromium. The websites are the same: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"`
20	  gives your agent the scouting logins in `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, the way a run gets its logins.
21	
22	### Several browsers
23	
24	To work on several websites at once, ask for up to four browsers in `agent.json`:
25	
26	```json
27	{"setup": ["npm", "ci"], "run": ["node", "agent.js"], "browsers": 2}
28	```
29	
30	Each is its own Chromium on its own screen (browser n on `DISPLAY=:n`), and `CDP_URLS` lists their CDP URLs in
31	order (`CDP_URL` stays the first). With Playwright:
32	
33	```javascript
34	import { chromium } from "playwright"
35	
36	const sites = JSON.parse(process.env.CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS)
37	const browsers = await Promise.all(JSON.parse(process.env.CDP_URLS).map((url) => chromium.connectOverCDP(url)))
38	const pages = browsers.map((browser) => browser.contexts()[0].pages()[0])
39	await Promise.all([pages[0].goto(sites[0].url), pages[1].goto(sites[1].url)])
40	```
41	
42	At most 4 browsers run at a time. Use tabs (`context.newPage()`) and browser contexts (`browser.newContext()`)
43	inside them as freely as you like, but don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included: the sandbox stops
44	them and says so in the run's logs. A test run shows its browsers side by side while it runs and keeps a recording
45	of each. Locally there is no `CDP_URLS`: on your machine your agent starts its own browsers.
46	
47	## Models
48	
49	The hosted models are free to use. Every run gets `QWEN_BASE_URL` and `QWEN_API_KEY` for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, an
50	OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls and images; on your machine `atira scout --env` sets the same variables,
51	pointed at `atira models proxy`. You can also bring your own key for any provider through the metering proxy;
52	[how cost is measured](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#how-cost-is-measured) has the details. After quality you are ranked on cost × time, so a cheaper model or a faster run that gets the answer right moves you
53	up.
54	
55	## What makes it hard, on purpose
56	
57	The websites are designed to trip agents up: cookie walls, flaky error pages that need a retry, expiring sessions
58	that send you back to the login, documents inside iframes and ZIP files, popups that close themselves, paging and
59	"load more" buttons, look-alike records, superseded versions shown first, a timezone that is not yours. Treat
60	every page as adversarial and verify what you read.
61	
62	## Tips
63	
64	- Read the brief's rules carefully: they define the one correct answer.
65	- Keep what the model reads small: page text without duplicated labels, only the parts you need.
66	- Use prompt caching for your system prompt and tool definitions.
67	- Re-read a page after every action that changes it; pages update asynchronously.
68	- Drive four browsers in parallel, one per website (`"browsers": 4`, see [Several browsers](#several-browsers)):
69	  reading the four sites at once speeds up each run and your iteration, at the cost of more complex code.
70	- Validate your answer against `answer_schema` before sending it; a `400` costs only time.
71	- Submit before the clock runs out: a scored run has 20 minutes (`expires_at` in the run). Every part of the answer
72	  scores on its own, so have your agent submit its best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
73	  searching; a run that ends without an answer scores 0.
74	- Develop against the public websites locally (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run`):
75	  a test run shows the full score breakdown, so use it to find what your agent gets wrong.
76	- Work the answer out from the websites: the final run, which weighs most for the winners, uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.
77	
78	## Starter kit
79	
80	[`starter-kit/`](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and
81	submits an answer, attaches to the run's browsers over CDP with Playwright, and shows one call to each hosted model.
82	Your agent goes in `solve()` in `agent.py`; out of the box it exits without an answer. Start from it or from scratch.
83	=== docs/run-contract.md
84	# How a run works
85	
86	> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).
87	
88	A run is one attempt at one scenario of one challenge. It starts with a run token, gives your agent a task and
89	logins for the challenge's websites, and ends when your agent submits its answer or time runs out. Test runs and
90	scored runs both run your package in the [sandbox](#scored-run); you develop on your own machine with the scouting
91	logins.
92	
93	## Develop locally, then test in the sandbox
94	
95	RFQ has one public scenario, `public-1`: the websites as you see them.
96	
97	1. **Develop locally** against the public websites with the scouting logins the organizers publish:
98	   `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` (in PowerShell: `atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`) sets
99	   `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` (the websites and their logins, the JSON a run gets), each website's URL as
100	   `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL`, and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, the `brief`, `access`, `submission` and `answer_schema` of
101	   `GET $API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting` as JSON (`CHALLENGE_SCOUTING_URL` is that address). There is no run token.
102	   Where the platform hosts models, they need no key: `--env` also exports each one's base URL and key, pointed at
103	   `atira models proxy` on your computer with `local` as the key, so run `atira login` once, then keep
104	   `atira models proxy` running in another terminal. Those calls are free, recorded and never ranked. Any other
105	   provider takes your own key.
106	   Nothing done with these logins counts.
107	   A bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting.
108	2. **Test in the sandbox:** `atira test-run ./my-agent` uploads your package, starts a test run on `public-1` and
109	   opens its run page live. It runs in the same sandbox as a scored run, but for up to 2 hours instead of 20 minutes (keep it under
110	   20 to be safe), and the run page shows its
111	   score with the full breakdown. `atira cancel` stops it early.
112	
113	## Inside a run
114	
115	1. **Read the task:** `GET $CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` with the header `x-api-key: $CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`
116	   returns:
117	   - `brief`: the task statement in markdown, with the rules;
118	   - `access`: one entry per website: `siteId`, `url`, and `credentials` (`username`, `password`);
119	   - `submission`: where the answer goes: `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` (POST it to that URL) or
120	     `{"kind": "site", "siteId": ..., "url": ...}` (submit it on that website, e.g. RFQ's configurator);
121	   - `answer_url` (API submissions only) and `answer_schema` (JSON Schema of the answer);
122	   - `started_at`, `expires_at`, and what the run has spent on LLM calls so far.
123	   - `llm_proxy_url`: the model proxy base with this run's token, `llm_providers` and `llm_base_urls` (each
124	     provider's proxy base), and `llm_env` (the SDK base-URL variables the run step gets).
125	   Keep the token secret: it is your agent's identity for this run.
126	2. **Work:** your agent logs into the websites with those credentials and collects what it needs. Its LLM calls
127	   go through our metering proxy: a hosted model's with the run token its key variable already holds, any other
128	   provider's with your own key (below).
129	3. **Answer** through the run's `submission` target. For an `api` target, `POST` the answer as JSON to
130	   `answer_url` with the same `x-api-key` header. For a `site` target, submit it on that website: the site
131	   forwards it to the platform, shows the same validation issues in German, and confirms with a receipt.
132	   - `400` with `issues`: the answer is malformed. Nothing is recorded, the clock keeps running, fix it and send
133	     it again.
134	   - `202`: accepted and final. The run ends, the token and the website logins stop working, and a test run
135	     returns its score and breakdown. Your agent then has 10 seconds to exit before the platform stops it.
136	
137	Site logins are issued per run and only work while that run is live. Send tokens in the `x-api-key` header
138	(`Authorization: Bearer` works too). Send a User-Agent of your own: the edge in
139	front of the API currently refuses Python's default `Python-urllib/…` agent with 403. Test runs last up to 2 hours.
140	
141	## LLM calls
142	
143	Use the [hosted models](#how-cost-is-measured), which are free, or bring your own key for any provider and model.
144	Every call goes through our proxy, which forwards it unchanged and only measures it: a provider you bring bills your
145	own key, and the ranking uses what the call costs at the published prices. A scored run's sandbox reaches only our
146	API and the challenge's websites, so its model calls work only through the proxy; test runs are metered the same way.
147	
148	The run token sits in the proxy path, so your key keeps its usual header and an SDK needs only a base URL:
149	
150	```
151	$API/llm/run/<run token>/<provider>/<the provider's own API path>
152	```
153	
154	`llm_proxy_url` is the run's proxy, `<run API>/llm/run/<run token>`; in a test or scored run it is `$LLM_PROXY_URL`. Built-in providers:
155	
156	| Provider | Forwards to | Base URL for its SDK or an OpenAI-compatible client |
157	| --- | --- | --- |
158	| `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
159	| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
160	| `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openrouter/v1` |
161	| `google` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google` (Gemini SDK), `…/google/v1beta/openai` |
162	| `groq` | `https://api.groq.com/openai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/groq/v1` (use an OpenAI client) |
163	| `mistral` | `https://api.mistral.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral/v1` |
164	| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/deepseek/v1` |
165	| `xai` | `https://api.x.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/xai/v1` (HTTP API; the gRPC `xai-sdk` cannot use the proxy) |
166	| `together` | `https://api.together.xyz` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
167	| `fireworks` | `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/fireworks/v1` |
168	
169	The organizers may add providers; `llm_providers` lists them all, the models the platform hosts itself included,
170	each under its own id with its base URL in `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`. Any path under a provider's base works
171	(messages, chat completions, responses, embeddings, model listings) with the request's method and body intact.
172	
173	### Your key
174	
175	Send your provider key the way the provider expects it: `x-api-key` (Anthropic), `Authorization: Bearer`
176	(OpenAI and compatible providers), `x-goog-api-key` or `?key=` (Gemini), or `api-key`. The proxy forwards it
177	unchanged and never stores, logs or returns it. For test and scored runs, keep it as a [team secret](#team-secrets),
178	not in your package: we store packages and the review agent reads them.
179	
180	With the base-URL variables set, the providers' SDKs need no changes: OpenAI's reads `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and sends
181	`OPENAI_API_KEY` as `Authorization: Bearer`, Anthropic's reads `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and sends `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
182	as `x-api-key`:
183	
184	```python
185	from openai import OpenAI
186	
187	client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY
188	```
189	
190	A client that cannot set the provider's own header may send the key as `x-provider-key`; the proxy forwards it in
191	the provider's header. For Google's Gemini SDK, set the HTTP base URL explicitly:
192	
193	```python
194	import os
195	from google import genai
196	
197	client = genai.Client(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"],
198	    http_options={"base_url": os.environ["LLM_PROXY_URL"] + "/google"})
199	```
200	
201	```javascript
202	import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"
203	
204	const client = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY,
205	  httpOptions: { baseUrl: process.env.LLM_PROXY_URL + "/google" } })
206	```
207	
208	A request without a key of its own gets `401` "Add your <provider> API key to the request.", unless the
209	organizers pay for that provider: then the proxy adds their key to a run's calls. In that case a scored run's
210	key variable for that provider (for example `OPENAI_API_KEY`) holds the run token as a placeholder, so SDKs
211	start, unless you have a team secret by that name; the proxy never forwards the token.
212	
213	**Development outside runs:** with your personal token you may use the proxy without a run, at
214	`$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the header `x-atira-team-key: <token>`, or at `$API/llm/team/<token>/<provider>/…`
215	(prefer the header: a token lasts 90 days, and URLs end up in logs). Bring your own key; this usage is recorded
216	for your team and never ranked. Older clients may still call `$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the run token in
217	`x-api-key` and the provider key in `x-provider-key`. Without a run token or personal token, the proxy answers
218	`401`.
219	
220	A request body may be up to 32 MiB (`413` above that), enough for several full-screen screenshots and a long
221	context.
222	
223	### How cost is measured
224	
225	Every call is recorded. Reported usage, including cached input and thinking tokens, is priced at each
226	provider's published per-token prices for that model, with any deployment-specific prices published by the organizers.
227	An upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. OpenRouter reports one for every call (send
228	`"usage": {"include": true}` with older clients), so models without a published price are accepted there; a call
229	that reports no cost is charged at the highest published price. Elsewhere, unpriced models and models outside
230	a configured allowlist are refused before forwarding. Streamed calls count too: the proxy asks OpenAI-compatible
231	providers for a stream's usage (`stream_options.include_usage`), so a streamed chat completion ends with one more
232	chunk with empty `choices` and the usage. A stream cut off before its usage, or one whose provider reports none, counts
233	an estimate from the text that arrived and from the request, about four characters per token; a client that hangs up
234	early is still billed for everything the provider sends. There is no spending limit. Model listings and other
235	endpoints without inference usage cost nothing; Anthropic `count_tokens` also costs nothing. All network and
236	fair-play rules still apply, including when using provider-side tools.
237	
238	The models the platform hosts itself (`GET /v1/models/status` lists them with their prices) are free to use, never
239	charged; each call counts toward your run's cost at simulated API prices, so the cost ranking stays honest.
240	
241	### Team secrets
242	
243	Team secrets are environment variables for your agent's run step in test runs and scored runs, such as
244	`OPENAI_API_KEY`. Manage them on the team page under Secrets, or with your personal token:
245	
246	```sh
247	curl -X PUT -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/json" \
248	  --data '{"value": "sk-…"}' "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
249	curl -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets"   # names and dates only
250	curl -X DELETE -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
251	```
252	
253	Values are encrypted, never shown again and redacted from run logs; saving a name again replaces its value.
254	Setup never receives them. Names are uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, and
255	cannot be platform variables (`CHALLENGE_*`, `*_BASE_URL`, `*_SERVER_URL`, `*_PROXY`, `LLM_PROXY_URL`,
256	`CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT`, `PATH`, `HOME`, `DISPLAY`, …). A team keeps at most 20; each value is 16 characters to 4 KB long.
257	
258	## Scored run
259	
260	Each scored submission runs once in the sandbox on the public dataset (RFQ's `public-1`) and is scored; that run
261	ranks on the leaderboard. The final run at the end of the hackathon uses the same sandbox on a private dataset (see
262	[Submitting](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md#what-happens-next)). Runs are created from your uploaded package. The sandbox is
263	a Linux VM with a desktop at 1280×800, a **headful Chromium** already open with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on
264	`127.0.0.1:9222` (or up to four, see [Browsers](#browsers)) and these toolchains, ready for your user:
265	
266	- **TypeScript and JavaScript:** Node 24 (runs `.ts` files directly), npm, pnpm and bun.
267	- **Python:** Python 3.12 and uv (`uv venv`, `uv pip install`, `uv run`); there is no system pip.
268	- **Rust:** stable Rust (1.99) with cargo. Fetch crates during setup; the run is offline except for the platform
269	  and the websites.
270	- gcc, make, git, curl and jq.
271	
272	1. **Setup (not counted toward your time, up to 5 minutes):** your `setup` command runs with network access but without any credentials, e.g. to install dependencies.
273	2. **Model warm-up (not counted toward your time):** the models the platform hosts itself, when it offers any, scale
274	   to zero when nobody uses them, and waking one takes one to eight minutes. The platform wakes them as soon as your
275	   run leaves the queue and starts your run only once they're warm (at most 10 minutes after setup), so a cold start
276	   never counts toward your time. The run's log says when they're warm. While runs are active, the platform keeps
277	   them warm. `"models"` in `agent.json` lists the ones your agent system calls, by their `provider` id from
278	   `GET /v1/models/status` (the start page shows it too); the run waits for those alone, and `"models": []` starts it
279	   right after setup:
280	
281	   ```json
282	   {"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "models": []}
283	   ```
284	
285	   Without it the run waits for every hosted model. Anything else, such as an unknown id, rejects the package with
286	   `Invalid agent.json: models: …` and the ids it takes. It decides only the wait: your run may call any hosted model
287	   whatever it lists, but one it didn't list may still be waking.
288	
289	   **If a hosted model fails mid-run:** retry failed calls, as with any provider; a short outage is yours to ride out.
290	   If our models were down for most of the run (from the first failed call on, a 5xx from our model or a lost
291	   connection to it, at least 8 in 10 of the run's hosted-model calls failed, over at least half its time) and the run
292	   then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count toward ranking or
293	   any limit, and a scored run starts again once by itself. A
294	   run that answered keeps its result.
295	3. **Run (timed):** your `run` command starts with this environment. The clock starts here.
296	
297	| Variable | Value |
298	| --- | --- |
299	| `CHALLENGE_API_URL` | the API; read your task at `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` |
300	| `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | the run token |
301	| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with this run's logins, as JSON: the same as `access` |

352	# Fair play
353	
354	**Rules at a glance**
355	
356	You submit an agentic system: one agent or several. In the sandbox it does the whole job on its own: finds what it needs on the four websites, works out the bid and submits it. Nobody helps it during a run.
357	
358	**Not allowed**
359	
360	- **Hardcoding:** copying values from the websites into your package (prices, material numbers, totals, discounts, logins, TANs), including in prompts and notes, also as defaults or fallbacks. Using what the task brief tells every team, like the sales director's mailbox, is fine.
361	- **Pre-solving:** working out the answer yourself, or having an AI assistant do it, and putting the result in your package. Exploring the sites with an assistant is fine.
362	- **Scripts instead of agents:** a fixed click path, or a crawler that grabs everything for one model call. A model has to choose where to go, what to search for and what matters.
363	- **Outside help during a run:** contacting anything besides our platform and the four websites, calling a model other than through our proxy (your own API keys work through it), running a model inside the sandbox, or starting your own browsers (use the up to 4 provided). Setup may install dependencies.
364	
365	**How it's checked:** an AI reviewer reads every submitted package before its scored run. Unclear cases are flagged and stay off the leaderboard until an organizer has looked. The final runs on websites and data your system hasn't seen.
366	
367	The details follow.
368	
369	## Allowed
370	
371	- Any agent design; the free hosted models, or any provider and model with your own key, through the proxy; any
372	  amount of tokens.
373	  The proxy forwards your calls unchanged and measures them: reported usage is metered at the published model
374	  prices, and an upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. See [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)
375	  for SDK configuration.
376	- Keeping your model key as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets) rather than in your package.
377	- Your own code, prompts and tools; open-source libraries installed during setup.
378	- Using what you learned with the scouting logins and in test runs about how the websites work.
379	- Up to 4 browsers at a time: ask for them with `"browsers"` in `agent.json` and use as many tabs and browser
380	  contexts inside them as you like.
381	
382	## Not allowed
383	
384	- Hardcoding values copied from the public scenario or its websites into code, config, prompts or notes, including defaults and fallbacks: tender references, material numbers, prices, totals, discounts, logins and TANs. Facts the task brief states for every scenario, such as the sales director's mailbox, are
385	  rules you may use.
386	- A scripted solution. Your agent system must be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the
387	  information and makes the decisions. Code can help it (browser control, parsing, arithmetic, checks, reading a
388	  page or document the model chose, paging through results it asked for), and several agents and browsers may work
389	  in parallel. Rejected: a fixed script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback,
390	  and a crawler that collects the websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
391	- Bundling or running a local model, or reaching any model other than through the proxy.
392	- Contacting hosts other than the API and the challenge's websites, or trying to get data out of the sandbox.
393	- Starting browsers of your own in the sandbox, headless ones included. At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up
394	  to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start others.
395	  On your own machine (developing with the scouting logins) your agent starts its own browsers; that is up to you.
396	- Attacking the platform, the websites, the sandbox or other teams; sharing scored-run data.
397	
398	## How it is checked
399	
400	- **Package review before any scored run:** an AI code reviewer, a coding agent that reads your whole package in an
401	  isolated VM. Outcomes: passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged package still runs and scores, but its
402	  result stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it
403	  marked "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Notes and docs addressed to the reviewer are not evidence of compliance
404	  and do not count against you on their own. Instructions trying to steer the reviewer's verdict do.
405	  The reviewer's reasons stay with the organizers: your team reads "Flagged by the reviewing agent" or "Rejected by
406	  the reviewing agent". Someone from Atira looks at flagged packages shortly and unflags a misdetection; if you think
407	  a reject is one, contact the Atira team.
408	- **The organizers decide flagged packages, and can look at any submission:** they pass it, add an internal note
409	  (this changes nothing you or the leaderboard see) or disqualify it. A disqualified submission and its runs read
410	  "disqualified": it leaves the leaderboard and the final run, its runs still going stop, and your team page shows the
411	  organizers' reason.
412	- **Hardcoded values:** the reviewer rejects copied scenario values in code or config, even in defaults or fallbacks.
413	- **The final run** uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a
414	  supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software,
415	  with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently
416	  across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it. That run weighs most when we pick the
417	  winners, so build a system that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario.
418	- **The sandbox** reaches only our API and the websites, so every model call passes the proxy and is measured.
419	  Your team secrets reach only the timed run step and are redacted from its logs.
420	- **Website logins** exist only for a live run and stop working when it ends.
421	- **Browsers:** the sandbox stops any browser your agent starts beyond the ones it asked for and notes it in the
422	  run's logs: `[platform] stopped a browser the agent started`.
423	- **Everything measured** (tokens, cost, time, the answer) is recorded by the platform, never reported by you.
424	
425	Breaking these rules gets the submission rejected before it runs, or removed later; repeated or deliberate attempts
426	get the team disqualified.
427	
428	## Flagged results
429	
430	A flagged result stays off the public leaderboard until an organizer passes it. **Show flagged** on the leaderboard
431	lists flagged results, without a rank.

434	
435	**Turn a public tender into a correct, signed bid without a person touching it.**
436	
437	You work for a German hydraulics manufacturer that wants to bid on a public tender for hydraulic cylinders. 523	## Public and private data
524	
525	There are two datasets. The leaderboard uses the public one, on these websites. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
526	
527	- **Public dataset:** The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too.
528	- **Private dataset (the final run):** When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario.
529	
530	## Bid rules
531	
532	The brief states these rules in full. Together they define exactly one correct answer.
533	
534	1. **Quantity:** The tender quantity, overridden by the latest clarification that changes that position.
535	2. **Requirement:** The position's requirement in the specification revision marked current.
536	3. **Material:** The active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification match exactly. If a position has none, the answer is no bid.
537	4. **Unit price:** The price condition valid on the scenario date, at the highest quantity scale reached, minus the approved discount, rounded half-up to the cent.
538	5. **Discount:** The most recent approval from the sales director for this exact tender; otherwise 0 %.
539	6. **Lead time:** The from-stock lead time when stock covers the quantity, otherwise the production lead time.
540	7. **Total:** The sum of quantity times unit price, rounded half-up to the cent.
541	8. **Decision:** Bid, with one entry per tender position; no bid with no positions and a total of 0 when a material is missing.
542	9. **Partial submission:** Full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
543	10. **Finding records:** The specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
544	11. **Agent requirement:** A language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
545	12. **Commercial clauses:** A tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
546	13. **Withdrawn answers:** A tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
547	14. **Scoped amendments:** After selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
548	15. **Shared stock:** Sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
549	16. **Conditional discount:** The latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
550	17. **Units:** Tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
551	18. **Pricing breakdown:** Base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
552	19. These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
553	20. **Technical derivation:** For a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
554	21. **Authority and time:** Resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
555	22. **Currency:** The valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
556	23. **Packaging:** Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
557	24. **Delivery:** Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
558	25. **Shared setup:** Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
559	26. **Project bonus:** The finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
560	27. **Final price:** Clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
561	28. **Metal indices:** Select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
562	29. **Scoring in bid cases:** Decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.
563	
564	## How a run works
565	
566	Develop on your machine against the public websites with the scouting logins (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox: `atira test-run` uploads your package, starts a test run and opens it live, or drop the package on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team). A test run lasts up to 2 hours on the public data and returns its score with the full breakdown. In the commands, `$ATIRA_TOKEN` holds your personal token (sign in with `atira login`, then `atira token`).
567	
568	1. **Start.** The run issues a token, the task brief and fresh logins for every website.
569	2. **Read.** Your agent reads the brief, the rules and the answer format from the API.
570	3. **Work the websites.** It works through the 4 websites in a real browser and gathers the facts.
571	4. **Submit.** It enters the bid in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with a TAN from the webmail.
572	5. **Scored.** The answer is checked against the one correct answer; quality, cost and time are recorded.
573	
574	### Develop locally
575	
576	```sh
577	eval "$(atira scout --challenge rfq --env)"   # logins for the public websites
578	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting"   # the same, with the brief, as JSON
579	# run your agent on your machine, then once in the sandbox:
580	atira test-run ./my-agent --challenge rfq
581	```
582	
583	`atira scout --env` exports the scouting logins as `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` (the shape a run gets), each website's URL, and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, the brief and the answer format. It also points the free hosted models at `atira models proxy` on your computer, so your agent needs no model key; another provider takes your own. Nothing done there counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. In a run, your agent reads the same at `GET /v1/runs/current` with the run token as `x-api-key`, and hands in one valid answer of up to 65,536 bytes; a malformed one returns its problems while the clock keeps running.
584	
585	### Read the run
586	
587	Inside a test or scored run, with the run token (`$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`) in `RUN_TOKEN`:
588	
589	```sh
590	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/current" -H "x-api-key: $RUN_TOKEN"
591	```
592	
593	The response holds `brief` (the task in Markdown, with the rules), `access` (each website's `url` and `credentials`), `submission` (where the answer goes), `answer_schema`, `expires_at`, `llm_proxy_url` and `llm_providers`. Outside a run, `GET /v1/challenges/rfq/scouting` returns the brief, logins, answer target and schema for the public websites, without a token.
594	
595	### In the sandbox
596	
597	A test run and a scored run start your `run` command with these variables. `setup` runs before, with network but without them, for up to 5 minutes that don't count toward your time.
598	
599	| Variable | Value |
600	| --- | --- |
601	| `CHALLENGE_API_URL` | the platform API; the run is at /v1/runs/current |
602	| `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | this run's token, sent as x-api-key |
603	| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with this run's logins, as JSON |
604	| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | the model proxy with the run token in its path; bring your own provider key |
605	| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/anthropic |
606	| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/openai/v1 |
607	| `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/google |
608	| `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/mistral |
609	| `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/together/v1 |
610	| `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY` | Clef through the proxy, https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/clef, with the run token as its key; free, no usage cap. |
611	| `QWEN_BASE_URL`, `QWEN_API_KEY` | Qwen through the proxy, https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/qwen/v1, with the run token as its key; free, no usage cap. |
612	| `CDP_URL` | the sandbox browser (Chrome DevTools Protocol), http://127.0.0.1:9222; with several, browser 1 |
613	| `CDP_URLS` | every browser's CDP URL in order, as a JSON array: one per browser asked for in agent.json, up to 4 |
614	| `BROWSER_COUNT` | how many browsers the sandbox started, 1 to 4 |
615	| `DISPLAY` | the desktop browser 1 runs on, :1 at 1280×800; browser n is on :n |
616	| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `http_proxy`, `https_proxy` | the only way out: the platform and the websites (http://127.0.0.1:3128) |
617	| `NO_PROXY`, `no_proxy` | reached directly, so the browser's CDP stays local (localhost,127.0.0.1) |
618	| `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` | Node's fetch uses the proxy (1) |
619	
620	Every model call goes through the platform's metering proxy, which records its tokens and cost; the hosted models need no key, and any other provider takes the team's own. [The run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls) has the key and SDK settings for each provider.
621	
622	## Unlimited Inference
623	
624	We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.
625	
626	### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
627	
628	#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.
629	
630	- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
631	- **Simulated pricing:**
632	  - Input: $0.15 / M tokens
633	  - Cached input: $0.016 / M tokens
634	  - Cache writes: Free
635	  - Output: $0.47 / M tokens
636	- **Precision:** [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) (NVIDIA's checkpoint)
637	
638	Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.
639	
640	```python
641	import os
642	from openai import OpenAI
643	
644	qwen = OpenAI(
645	    base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
646	    api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
647	)
648	reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
649	    model="qwen",
650	    messages=[{
651	        "role": "user",
652	        "content": "Which button submits?",
653	    }],
654	)
655	```
656	
657	### Cloudflare Clef
658	
659	A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: `choice` picks one of your options, `noul` gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and `score` rates on a scale you set. See [Cloudflare's announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/) and [the benchmarks](https://clef-evals.workers-ai-mle.workers.dev). Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.
660	
661	- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 16 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
662	- **Simulated pricing:**
663	  - Input: $0.24 / M tokens
664	  - Output: Not priced
665	
666	Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.
667	
668	```sh
669	curl "$CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide" \
670	  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLEF_API_KEY" \
671	  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
672	  "state": {"page": "Checkout returns 502"},
673	  "questions": {"next": {
674	    "type": "choice",
675	    "instructions": "What next?",
676	    "criteria": {
677	      "retry": "Retry the request",
678	      "report": "Report the error"}}}}'
679	```
680	
681	In a run, `QWEN_BASE_URL` with `QWEN_API_KEY` and `CLEF_BASE_URL` with `CLEF_API_KEY` are set for you. On your machine, `atira models proxy` serves the same APIs on 127.0.0.1, so the same code works in both. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. An idle model can take several minutes to wake on its first call, so use long timeouts.
682	
683	```sh
684	atira login   # once per computer
685	atira models proxy   # keep it running; it prints:
686	export QWEN_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1
687	export QWEN_API_KEY=local
688	export CLEF_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/clef
689	export CLEF_API_KEY=local
690	```
691	
692	Cost and time count toward your rank, and a call to these models costs a fraction of a frontier call. Use them for the easy steps.
693	
694	If one fails mid-run, retry the call, as with any provider. If they were down for most of a run that then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count, and a scored run starts again once by itself.
695	
696	## Submitting
697	
698	A submission is your agent as a gzipped tarball. It is reviewed automatically, then run once in the sandbox on the public dataset, and that score ranks your team. Submit as often as you like, one at a time; your best submission holds your place on the leaderboard, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run.
699	
700	### agent.json
701	
702	```json
703	{
704	  "setup": ["uv", "sync"],
705	  "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"],
706	  "models": ["qwen"]
707	}
708	```
709	
710	Put `agent.json` at the root of the tarball, next to your code and its dependency file. Up to 20 MB compressed. `setup` installs dependencies with network access, within 5 minutes that don't count toward your time; `run` is timed and reaches only the platform and the websites. `"browsers": 1–4` (default 1) is how many browsers the sandbox starts, each on its own screen. `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls; the run waits only for those to warm up (for all of them when it's absent). Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, and Rust with cargo are installed. The [starter kit](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal skeleton to start from.
711	
712	### Upload
713	
714	```sh
715	tar czf agent.tar.gz -C my-agent .
716	curl --data-binary @agent.tar.gz \
717	  -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" \
718	  -H "content-type: application/gzip" \
719	  "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions"
720	```
721	
722	Or drop the tarball on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team). Upload it as a test run first to watch it work in the sandbox: its browser live, its logs, and a recording afterwards.
723	
724	### Test run first
725	
726	The same tarball as a test run: one run in the scored-run sandbox on the public data, with live browser frames, logs and a recording.
727	
728	```sh
729	tar czf agent.tar.gz -C my-agent .
730	curl --data-binary @agent.tar.gz \
731	  -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" \
732	  -H "content-type: application/gzip" \
733	  "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/rehearsals"
734	```
735	
736	### Follow your submissions
737	
738	```sh
739	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
740	```
741	
742	Logs of test runs and scored runs, from a cursor (`after`); repeat with the returned `cursor` until `chunks` is empty:
743	
744	```sh
745	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs?after=0" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
746	```
747	
748	## Scoring and ranking
749	
750	Every submission is measured on its run in the sandbox.
751	
752	- **Quality:** 0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.
753	- **Eligibility:** The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.
754	- **Cost:** Every model call goes through the proxy and is priced per model. There is no budget: at equal quality, cost × time decides.
755	- **Time:** Wall-clock time from the start of the run until the answer is accepted. It weighs as much as cost: halving either halves cost × time.
756	
757	Order: Eligible first → Quality ↓ → Cost × time ↑.
758	
759	Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.
760	
761	## Leaderboard
762	
763	**Public dataset.** Eligible first, then quality, then cost × time. The top ten; the [full leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md) has every team.
764	
765	| # | Team | Members | Quality | Cost | Time | Subm. |
766	| ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
767	| 1 | [Here for the Memes](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/teams/team_83680a10ba1d0069.md) | Cryoxtom, ffaex, megib16, codebyharshit | 21.5 | $0.3839 | 00:16:24 | 3 |
768	| 2 | [Adira](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/teams/team_b9529d66d3371f26.md) (not eligible) | yueouLi, vlad-moroshan, KFX5314, mo-first, OmranKaddah | 0 | $0.00 | 00:00:02 | 4 |
769	| 3 | [Ctrl+Alt+Del](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/teams/team_197dcaa11e155b34.md) (not eligible) | simonroehrl, sadnyani-4, VincInfo | 0 | $0.00 | 00:00:03 | 1 |
770	| 4 | [EliTUM](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/teams/team_3b6cce9770611455.md) (not eligible) | SashaKrotova, SzP42, leodevpt, iiisak, geapdev | 0 | $0.1025 | 00:19:26 | 1 |
771	
772	## Fair play
773	
774	Your agent has to find the answer itself.
775	
776	- Your system must work the answer out from the websites at run time, with a model doing the navigating and deciding. A coding agent reviews every package; hardcoded answers, fixed scripts and crawlers are rejected.
777	- Bring your own model key for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks, kept as a team secret. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. The sandbox reaches the platform and the websites, nothing else.
778	- At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up to 4 in agent.json ("browsers"), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included. The sandbox stops any other browser your agent starts.
779	- One submission in flight per team. Submit again once it has finished.
780	
781	Rules at a glance: [Fair play](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md)
782	
783	## The answer format
784	
785	The configurator on the tender portal collects exactly this answer; the run's brief carries the same schema.
786
